Privacy by Design

Recording the process does not mean storing customer data.

Enterprise IT policy normally forbids retaining end-customer sensitive information. Our answer is not that an AI will try to blur it after the fact — masking happens at the source, before capture; raw frames are never written to disk; nothing leaves your network. What auditors review is the architecture, not a model accuracy rate.

Masked at sourceRaw frames never storedStays inside your networkYour team holds the review gate

Two Questions Before We Talk Solutions

Both answers point in the same direction: what is missing is not effort or intelligence — it is structured, machine-readable enterprise knowledge.

Question 1 — Can You Actually Document Your SOPs?

Everyone says:

"We already have a complete SOP library."

But reality is probably:

  • SOPs don't cover 100% of real-world scenarios.
  • SOPs have long since diverged from how agents actually work.
  • After 2 months of training, new hires still can't explain or execute properly.
  • Every veteran has an undocumented "personal SOP" in their head.
This is why screen recording matters. It is not about surveillance — it is the only reliable way to capture what agents actually do, turning "impossible to document" SOPs into visible, executable, reusable ontologies.

Question 2 — AI Isn't Dumb. It Just Doesn't Know Your Business.

Ask AI

"What is the average income in Beijing?"

It knows. General knowledge — it is everywhere online.

Ask AI

"What was my income last year?"

It doesn't know. Private enterprise data — no one ever fed it.

AI does not lack capability — it lacks your enterprise's private knowledge. Accumulated SOPs, business exceptions, company policies — these valuable assets sit scattered across employees' heads and personal notebooks, never converted into a form AI can use. OntoDesk's job is to turn private knowledge into ontologies and feed them to AI.

SOP Ontology: Making Knowledge Executable, Traceable and Evolvable

Raw SOP documents → structured ontology nodes → knowledge assets directly callable by AI agents.

❌ Problems with Traditional SOPs

  • Word/PDF documents — machines cannot understand them.
  • Updates are out of sync; conflicting versions circulate.

  • New staff cannot quickly search or execute them.

→

✅ Advantages of Ontology-Based SOPs

  • Structured nodes — AI can query and reason in real time.
  • Version-controlled, activated after human review.
  • Scenario coverage continuously monitored and filled.
  • New staff retrieve the correct steps in seconds.
  • Source-traceable; every piece of knowledge is evidence-backed.
Knowledge freshness: each SOP carries an expiry field — when it expires, human review is triggered automatically. Conflict detection: before new knowledge is written, the LLM cross-checks existing rules to prevent contradictions.

Privacy & Compliance: Record the Process, Not the Data

The hardest objection to screen recording is not technical, it is an IT policy one: customer-sensitive information must never be retained. We answer it by making retention structurally impossible, rather than promising that a model will catch everything.

01
Mask at Source
Everything masked by default, whitelist opens
→
02
Redact On Device
Pixels replaced before encoding, frames stay in memory
→
03
Never Leaves the Network
Whole pipeline runs inside your environment
→
04
Customer Review Gate
Your people approve before anything is exported
The design rule: a masking model can only ever be measured by its miss rate, and no one can defend a miss rate to an auditor. An architecture in which raw frames are never persisted and never leave the network can be inspected, tested and signed off.

Why Not Simply Detect and Blur?

Detect-and-blur is a blacklist: it has to find every sensitive item to be safe. Masking at source is a whitelist: it has to be told what is safe to show.

❌ Detect and Blur (blacklist)

  • Recall can never be proven to be 100%.
  • A single missed frame is a complete leak.
  • Free-text fields, ID photos, signatures and maps defeat OCR.
  • Liability lands on the vendor instead of on a policy.
  • Auditors have nothing verifiable to approve.
→

✅ Structurally Impossible (whitelist)

  • Masked before capture, so there is nothing to miss.
  • Raw frames are never written to disk in any form.
  • The rule list is explicit, readable and signed off by your IT.
  • Verification targets the architecture, not model accuracy.
  • Your team keeps the final call on every export.
Auditors can approve an architecture. They cannot approve a recall rate.

Three Layers, Matched to What Agents Actually Use

Most agent work happens in your own web systems, where masking is deterministic. Desktop software is handled through the accessibility layer. AI detection is only the safety net, never the primary control.

01

Web Systems · the majority

Element-level masking in the DOM. Every text node and input is masked by default; only whitelisted, non-sensitive containers are captured at all. This is a deterministic rule, not a model prediction — and the whitelist itself is a document your IT can review line by line.

02

Desktop Software · the remainder

Windows UI Automation and macOS Accessibility expose control type and position, so masking follows the control rather than the pixels. No OCR involved, so scrolling, small fonts and low contrast cannot break it. Unmapped controls are masked by default.

03

Safety Net · fail-closed

Keyframe OCR plus pattern and entity matching, with ID-card, face and signature detection. Below the confidence threshold the region is fully masked rather than released, and every detection dilates in both time and space so a fast scroll cannot expose a frame.

What Survives the Pipeline

Follow one recording from capture to ontology and watch the sensitive layer disappear at the first step and never come back.

01
Capture
Already masked at the source
→
02
On-Device Parsing

→
03
Structured SOP
Steps and branches, no business values
→
04
Raw Video Purged
Auto-deleted on a customer-set window, customer-held keys
→
05
Ontology
Process knowledge only, PII-free by design
The key point: what enters the SOP and the ontology is process structure — which system, which control, which branch, in what order — not business data — who the customer is, which order number, which address. SOPs and ontologies never needed PII to do their job, so removing it costs nothing in accuracy.

Mapped Line by Line to Your IT Policy

The clauses below are the ones that usually block a recording deployment. Each maps to a control that can be demonstrated during the POC.

Policy requirementHow OntoDesk satisfies it
No customer-sensitive data may be retainedMasking is applied before encoding, so raw frames never reach storage in any form.
Data must not leave the corporate networkFully on-premise deployment, models included — the pipeline makes no external calls.
Processing must be auditableA signed masking rule list, complete processing logs, and sampled playback for your reviewers.
Collection must be minimal and necessaryOnly whitelisted business windows are captured; personal and non-work applications are skipped automatically.
Collection must be revocableAgents and administrators can pause capture at any moment and delete any time range afterwards.
Accountability must sit with the data ownerYour IT owns the rule list and your reviewers release every export — the vendor never decides what counts as sensitive.
For the POC: the fastest route through review is to validate the full pipeline on a masked or synthetic-data environment first, prove the capture-to-ontology chain end to end, and only then switch the same deployment onto production data once the rule list has been signed off.
